correctness.rationale: A fresh exact-rational exhaustive reconstruction over all \(24^4=331{,}776\) labeled strict profiles independently recomputed random priority from all 24 serial-dictatorship orders, probabilistic serial by exact eating-time arithmetic, ordinal efficiency using the Bogomolnaia-Moulin acyclicity criterion, and stochastic dominance by every rank cutoff. The resulting four-way counter was exactly \((72{,}288,190{,}512,57{,}312,11{,}664)\), which sums to the full profile space; the two ordinally-inefficient subclasses sum to 68,976 and \(11{,}664/68{,}976=81/479\). The primary Bogomolnaia-Moulin text was read at Lemma 3 and at its four-agent RP/PS example, confirming the criterion and the first nontrivial setting used by the census.
correctness.risk: The theorem is a finite exact census; correctness depends on the independently reconstructed definitions matching the standard RP, PS, ordinal-efficiency and stochastic-dominance conventions, which were checked against the primary sources.
sources: Bogomolnaia-Moulin, Journal of Economic Theory 100 (2001), Lemma 3 and four-agent RP/PS examples

originality.rationale: The primary literature establishes that random priority can be ordinally inefficient, gives explicit four-agent examples, and proves general dominance/contract and asymptotic prevalence results. It does not give the complete \(24^4\) four-agent partition, the exact 11,664 direct-PS-dominance count, or the \(81/479\) share. A same-round companion census determines the total RSD-inefficient count and symmetry refinements but does not contain the RP-versus-PS four-way partition; therefore it does not imply the final claim.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed computational enumeration of four-agent assignment profiles could exist under different terminology; no such source was located in bounded searches.

value.rationale: Four agents are the first nontrivial size for the direct PS-over-RP phenomenon identified by the foundational paper. The exact decomposition separates mere ordinal inefficiency from inefficiency witnessed by the canonical PS mechanism and quantifies the gap sharply, making this a natural finite boundary classification rather than an arbitrary computation.
value.risk: The result is finite and does not itself provide an asymptotic theory; its value is the exact first-nontrivial boundary census.

final_claim: In the balanced strict four-agent/four-object random-assignment problem, the exact labeled-profile census for random priority versus probabilistic serial is: equality on 72,288 profiles; distinct with random priority ordinally efficient on 190,512; random priority ordinally inefficient without direct probabilistic-serial dominance on 57,312; and direct probabilistic-serial stochastic dominance on 11,664. Hence random priority is ordinally inefficient on 68,976 of the 331,776 profiles, and direct probabilistic-serial dominance explains exactly \(81/479\) of those inefficient cases.
limitations: Balanced four-agent/four-object problems with complete strict preferences and uniform random priority only.
The census does not extend by itself to weak preferences, unequal numbers of agents and objects, or larger markets.
